title: Japanese Newspaper Kainichi Alleges That A Communist Leaders Has Been Established In French Concession

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
File No. D. REC S
No. S. B. D. 271
S.1, Special Branch Station,
Date April 22, 1936

Subject Japanese Newspaper "Mainichi" alleges that a Communist
headquarters has been established in French Concession.

Made by D.I. Sih Ju-liang Forwarded by W. Kuncar IS

The "Mainichi", a Japanese newspaper, published on
April 11, 1936, a report alleging that two Chinese named Fong
Hsiao-hui (方曉輝) and Chu Ming-sung (周明生), had formed
an "Ex-soldiers National Salvation Association" with
headquarters in the French Concession and were engaging in
anti-Japanese and communistic activities. Exhaustive
enquiries have been made with a view to confirming this
report but nothing can be learned to substantiate it.

It is to be noted that the "Nippo" on March 29, 1936,
published a report alleging that the authorities of the
French Concession were permitting agents of Soviet Russia to
establish headquarters in the Concession for the purpose of
conducting communist and anti-Japanese activities. A
declaration refuting this allegation was issued by the French
Consul-General on March 31, 1936, and published in local
foreign newspapers of April 1, 1936. In the same column,
Mr. Seiicki Uyeda, Chief of the Police Section of the
Japanese Consulate-General also issued a statement repudiating
the allegation, and on the contrary, expressing his satisfaction
with the French Authorities for their readiness in suppressing
anti-Japanese agitation.

报告
上海公共租界
档案号 D. REC S
编号 S. B. D. 271
S.1，特科分站，
日期 1936年4月22日

主题：日本报纸《每日新闻》称法租界内已设立共产党总部。

由督察 Sih Ju-liang（音译）制作 经 W. Kuncar 转呈

日本报纸《每日新闻》于1936年4月11日刊登一则报道，声称两名华人方曉輝（Fong Hsiao-hui）和周明生（Chu Ming-sung）组建了一个“退伍军人救国协会”，总部设在法租界，并从事反日及共产主义活动。为证实该报道，已进行详尽调查，但未能获取任何证据予以佐证。

值得注意的是，《日日新闻》（Nippo）于1936年3月29日刊登报道，声称法租界当局允许苏联代理人以开展共产主义和反日活动为目的在租界内设立总部。法国总领事于1936年3月31日发表声明驳斥这一指控，并于1936年4月1日刊登在当地外文报纸上。在同一栏目中，日本总领事馆警务课课长上田清吉（Seiicki Uyeda，音译）先生也发表声明否认该指控，相反，他对法国当局积极镇压反日煽动活动表示满意。

April II, 1936. Morning Translation.

MAINICHI (10-4-36)

RED ARMY IN SHANSI RECRUITING SOLDIERS IN SHANGHAI

It has been already reported
that a secret agreement has been concluded between Chiang
Kai Shek and the red army which has entered Shansi. The
Government army has also entered Shansi to destroy Yen Shi
Shan's power and to oppose Japan.
The secretariat of the Chinese
Communist Party in Shanghai is reported to have ordered
the red army in Shansi to create disturbances in Hopei,
Charhar and Suiyuan Provinces. The red army in Shansi
has requested the Shanghai armed People's Committee to
recruit a large number of soldiers. The head of the
Committee is reported to be one Huang Sin Hsiang.
be Applicants must have anti-
Japanese spirit, not less than 20 and not more than 30
years of age and are not members of the Blue Shirts Society.

HEADQUARTERS OF ANTI JAPANESE AND COMMUNIST ORGANIZATION
ESTABLISHED IN THE FRENCH CONCESSION

It is reported that Fong Hsiao
Huei, president of the Ex-soldiers National Salvation
Association formed by a number of unemployed soldiers, is
engaged in anti-Japanese activities. Another Chinese
named Chu Ming Sung, member of the Third International,
who had been co-operating with Fong Hsiao Huei, had some 方曉輝
trouble with Fong and since then Chu Ming Sung has become
the president of the Association. 周明生
Chu has established the
Headquarters of the Association in the French Concession
from where he will direct anti-Japanese and communistic
activities.

JAPANESE NAVY ASSOCIATION TO HOLD MEETING

The local Japanese Navy
Association will hold its annual meeting at the Japanese
Club at 1 p.m. April 15 to consider the budget for 1936
and the report on the year 1935.

NEW COUNSELLOR TO JAPANESE EMBASSY IN CHINA

A Domei telegram from Tokyo
reports that Mr. G. Morishima, Secretary of the Foreign Office,
has been appointed Counsellor to the Japanese Embassy in China.

NICHI-NICHI

JAPANESE AMALGAMATED ASSOCIATION OF STREET UNIONS
TO HOLD MEETING

The Standing Committee of the
Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions will hold
a meeting at its office at 4 p.m. April 13 to consider
the question of electricity service on extension roads and
the transfer of that service from the Shanghai Power Company
to the Chapei Electricity Company.

1936年4月11日。晨间翻译。

《每日新闻》（1936年4月10日）

山西红军在上海招募士兵

此前已有报道称，蒋介石与进入山西的红军达成了秘密协议。政府军也已进入山西，旨在摧毁阎锡山的势力并对抗日本。
据报道，中国共产党上海秘书处已命令山西红军在河北、察哈尔和绥远省制造骚乱。山西红军已请求上海武装人民委员会招募大量士兵。据报该委员会负责人为黄辛祥（Huang Sin Hsiang，音译）。
申请人必须具备反日精神，年龄不小于20岁且不大于30岁，且非蓝衣社成员。

反日及共产主义组织总部在法租界设立

据报道，由多名失业军人组成的“退伍军人救国协会”主席方曉輝（Fong Hsiao Huei）正从事反日活动。另一名华人周明生（Chu Ming Sung），系第三国际成员，曾与方曉輝合作，后与方发生纠纷，此后周明生成为该协会主席。
周已在法租界设立协会总部，并将由此指挥反日及共产主义活动。

日本海军协会将举行会议

本地日本海军协会将于4月15日下午1时在日本俱乐部举行年度会议，审议1936年预算及1935年度报告。

日本驻华使馆新任参赞

来自东京的同盟社电报报道称，外务省秘书森岛（G. Morishima，音译）先生已被任命为日本驻华使馆参赞。

《日日新闻》

日本街道工会联合会将举行会议

日本街道工会联合会常务委员会将于4月13日下午4时在其办事处举行会议，审议延伸道路电力服务问题以及将该服务从上海电力公司移交至闸北电气公司的事宜。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 1, 1936

JAPANESE POLICE
DENY RUMOURS

French Co-operation Is
Appreciated Here By
Consular Force

A report that "the authorities
of the French Concession are
closing their eyes to the activi-
ties of ... subversive elements,"
following the conclusion of the
Franco-Soviet Treaty of mutual
assistance, was effectively spiked
yesterday morning by Mr. S.
Uyeda, Chief of the Police Sec-
tion of the Japanese Consulate-
General here.
The report, emanating in
Tokyo, was distributed locally on
Saturday night by a Japanese
news agency, not Domei, and was
published in Sunday's morning
Japanese newspapers.
"I don't know where this in-
formation was obtained," Mr.
Uyeda told Domei in an exclusive
interview. "Those of us who are
engaged in police work here give
no credence to the report.
"On the contrary, we are deeply
indebted to the authorities of the
French Concession for their as-
sistance in suppressing the anti-
Japanese agitation in the Con-
cession and the protection of
Japanese residents there.
"The French authorities have
always been ready to apprehend
persons sought by us and to hand
them over to the Japanese Con-
sulate-General.
"Thanks to the mutual police
assistance, we have observed a
noticeable improvement in the
situation.
"I am issuing this statement,"
Mr. Uyeda concluded, "for fear
that some Japanese residents
here might be misled by such a
rumour."

2/1

《字林西报》，1936年4月1日，星期三

日本警方
否认谣言

领事警务队
在此感谢法国方面的合作

有关“继《法苏互助条约》签订后，法租界当局对……颠覆分子的活动视而不见”的报道，于昨日上午被驻沪日本总领事馆警务课课长上田（S. Uyeda）先生有效辟谣。
该报道源自东京，于周六晚间由一家日本通讯社（非同盟社）在当地分发，并刊登于周日的日本晨报上。
“我不知道这些消息是从何处获得的，”上田先生在接受同盟社独家采访时说。“我们这些在此从事警务工作的人对该报道不予采信。
“相反，我们深切感激法租界当局在协助镇压租界内的反日煽动活动以及保护当地日本居民方面提供的帮助。
“法国当局一直乐于逮捕我们要找的人员，并将其移交给日本总领事馆。
“得益于警方的相互协助，我们观察到局势有了明显改善。
“我发表此声明，”上田先生总结道，“是担心在沪的一些日本居民可能被此类谣言误导。”

2/1
